items.description_verbatim: Includes table of boundaries and Surveyor Generals' certifications.. From: U.S. District Court. California, Southern District. Land case 317 SD; land case map E-1362A (Bancroft Library).. Shows drainage, survey markers, boundaries, lot numbers, township lines, adjoining ranchos, Mission San Luis Rey, etc.. 4362 S35. Pen-and-ink on tracing cloth.
items.extent_verbatim: 1 ms. map ; on sheet 56 x 78 cm.
items.visual_confirmation: Cartouche on the map itself reads: 'PLAT of the Rancho SANTA MARGARITA Y LAS FLORES finally confirmed to PIO PICO et al. Surveyed under instructions from the U.S. SURVEYOR GENERAL by Max Strobel Dep. Sur. July 1867. Containing 89,742 acres.' This independently corroborates the title, surveyor and 1867 survey date. Sheet shows township/range grid (T8S-T11S, R4W-R7W), a boundaries table, a U.S. Surveyor General's certification, and an adjoining rancho labeled 'Rancho Mission Vieja or La Paz' along the northern edge. 'Santa Margarita Ranch House' is labeled within the grant. A digitization colour-calibration target is present along the bottom edge of the scan, outside the map sheet.
items.certification_date_note: The handwritten certifications on the sheet carry later dates than the survey: one is dated 'June 11th 1868' and another references 1870. The repository nonetheless assigns the item the date 1867 (the survey date). Recorded as stated; not reconciled.
items.resolution_note: 1500x1155 is the ONLY file the repository record offers (stated size 188.0 kB; downloaded 187,953 bytes, exact match). No IIIF endpoint resolved on digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu.

items.description_verbatim: Trabuco Mesa Adobe on Rancho Canada de Los Alisos, 1930. A few walls of the adobe stand in a field. It had a tile roof and was a sub-station of the San Juan Capistrano Mission where farming and cattle raising took place. "The building was made with three large rooms in a row, east to west; with the west room of different and evidently of later construction."
items.visual_confirmation: The photographic print itself carries the handwritten inscription 'Trabuco adobe 1930' across the sky at the top of the image, independently corroborating BOTH the subject identification and the 1930 date stated in the catalogue record. Image shows a long, low ruined adobe wall of roughly a dozen standing eroded piers/wall segments in open flat grassland, with a low tree line at left and distant hills at right. No roof survives.
items.location_note: Repository places this adobe on 'Rancho Canada de Los Alisos', NOT on Rancho Trabuco. The repository's own association is with Mission San Juan Capistrano (as a sub-station). Recorded as stated; not reconciled.

no_1912_plat.conclusion: NO 1912 plat map of Rancho Santa Margarita y Las Flores was found in any accessible repository. The 1867 Max Strobel plat was downloaded instead and is labeled 1867.
queries_run: loc.gov/search/?q=Rancho+Santa+Margarita&fo=json - 6935 hits, no 1912 plat; top relevant hit was HABS ca0579
davidrumsey.com luna API q=Santa+Margarita - 7 results, none a rancho plat
davidrumsey.com luna API q=Las+Flores - 6 results, all unrelated (Mexican maritime charts)
archive.org advancedsearch q="Santa Margarita y Las Flores" - 3 hits, all audio/video
WebSearch: 1912 plat map "Rancho Santa Margarita y Las Flores" - no 1912 item surfaced
no_1912_plat.blocked: BLM GLO (glorecords.blm.gov) could NOT be searched. All legacy endpoints return HTTP 401; the current site is a Salesforce Lightning SPA whose search redirects to Login.gov authentication. No account was created (prohibited). GLO survey-plat holdings for this rancho therefore remain UNVERIFIED - this is the single most likely remaining home for a 1912-dated survey plat and should be checked manually by a signed-in user.
no_1912_plat.structural_note: Ranchos were private land grants confirmed via US District Court land cases; their plats live in the land case files (Bancroft / NARA) rather than in the GLO public-land township plat series. A 1912 date would postdate the 1879 patent, so any 1912 document is more likely a partition or subdivision map than a US Surveyor General plat.

access_notes.calisphere_and_oac: curl/WebFetch receive HTTP 202 with an empty body (bot gate). oac.cdlib.org and content.cdlib.org 301-redirect into the same gate. A rendered browser session works. Calisphere image endpoints (/clip/, /crop/) DO serve to curl when given a browser User-Agent and a Referer header.
access_notes.usc: digitallibrary.usc.edu returns HTTP 403 to curl/WebFetch. Images are delivered as time-expiring CloudFront signed URLs captured from a rendered browser session.
access_notes.berkeley: digicoll.lib.berkeley.edu HTML pages return HTTP 202 to curl, but the /record/<id>/files/<name> download path serves normally to curl.
access_notes.loc: loc.gov and tile.loc.gov work with curl. Large TIFF downloads may truncate silently - one 16 MB master initially returned only 7,234 bytes with HTTP 200; always compare the byte count against the size stated in the item JSON and retry with --retry / -C -.
access_notes.contentdm: cdm16838.contentdm.oclc.org serves both the dmwebservices JSON API and IIIF endpoints to curl without restriction.
